title: Ocular Lymphoma: Mastering the Great Masquerader
summary: A comprehensive guide to Ocular Lymphoma, spanning Primary Vitreoretinal Lymphoma (PVRL) and Ocular Adnexal Lymphoma (OAL). Essential for identifying this lethal 'masquerader' and managing both intraocular and adnexal manifestations.

sections.title: Clinical Definition & Overview
sections.content: Ocular lymphoma is a heterogeneous group of malignancies. Primary Vitreoretinal Lymphoma (PVRL) is the most common intraocular form, typically a high-grade Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL). It is considered a subset of Primary CNS Lymphoma (PCNSL), with 60-80% of PVRL patients eventually developing CNS involvement. Ocular Adnexal Lymphoma (OAL) involves the orbit, lacrimal gland, or conjunctiva and is usually a low-grade B-cell MALT lymphoma.

sections.title: The 'Masquerader' Warning
content: Vitreous cells that are non-responsive to topical or systemic steroids.
Painless vitritis in an elderly patient without sign of infection.
Presence of creamy yellow-white sub-retinal infiltrates.
Rapid recurrence of 'uveitis' after tapering therapy.
New-onset neurological deficits or unexplained cognitive changes.

branches: MYD88 L265P Mutation (90% of PVRL cases)

sections.title: Clinical Features of PVRL
content: Vitreous: 'Aurora Borealis' effect (cells aligned along vitreous fibrils).
Vitreous clumps, sheets, or large grey-white debris.
Retina: Multifocal, sub-retinal yellow-white infiltrates.
Leopard Skinning: Reticular pigmentary changes over resolving infiltrates.
Minimal aqueous cell despite significant vitritis.
Usually painless with progressive floaters and blurred vision.

sections.title: Ocular Adnexal Lymphoma (OAL) Signs
content: Salmon-patch: Fleshy, pink, forniceal conjunctival mass.
Orbital: Painless proptosis or globe displacement.
Motility: Mechanical restriction and diplopia.
Lacrimal Gland: S-shaped ptosis and temporal mass.
Rubber-like consistency on palpation.

sections.title: Diagnostic Investigation Protocol
content: Step 1: Clinical Suspicion - Elderly patient with persistent vitritis.
Step 2: Neuroimaging - Contrast-enhanced MRI Brain & Orbits to rule out PCNSL.
Step 3: Tissue Diagnosis - Diagnostic Pars Plana Vitrectomy (25G/27G). Ensure 'dry' tap 1st.
Step 4: Specimen Handling - Immediate processing in CytoLyt; cells are fragile.
Step 5: Cytology & Flow - Look for high N:C ratio, pleomorphism, and B-cell markers.
Step 6: Biomarkers - Analyze IL-10 vs IL-6 levels (Ratio > 1.0 is highly suggestive).
Step 7: Molecular Testing - PCR for MYD88 L265P mutation and IGH rearrangement.
Step 8: Staging - Lumbar Puncture (Cytology) and PET-CT scan for systemic spread.

branches: White Dot Syndromes: APMPPE, Serpiginous Choroiditis

sections.title: Management: PVRL Treatment
content: Induction: Intravitreal Methotrexate (400µg/0.1mL) 2x weekly for 4 weeks.
Consolidation: Intravitreal Methotrexate 1x weekly for 8 weeks.
Maintenance: Intravitreal Methotrexate 1x monthly for 9 months.
Adjunct: Intravitreal Rituximab (1mg/0.1mL) for resistant cases.
Radiation: External Beam Radiation (EBRT) 30-40 Gy if systemic chemo not possible.
Systemic: High-dose Methotrexate (HD-MTX) + Rituximab if CNS/Systemic positive.

content.explanation: IL-10 is the key biomarker. IL-10 levels > IL-6 levels (Ratio >1) is the 'ten-ten' rule for identifying Ocular Lymphoma.

sections.title: Management: Adnexal Lymphoma (OAL)
content: Gold Standard: Involved-field Radiation Therapy (24-30 Gy).
Antibiotics: Doxycycline (100mg BID x 3 weeks) if Chlamydia psittaci suspected (MALT).
Monoclonal Antibodies: Intralesional or systemic Rituximab.
Observation: 'Watch and Wait' for very slow-growing asymptomatic MALT.
Surgical: Excision for small localized conjunctival lesions.

rows: Radiation Cataract, Radiation Retinopathy, Neovascular Glaucoma
High rate in PVRL; requires lifelong monitoring

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Always stop steroids 2 weeks before a diagnostic vitrectomy to avoid 'vanishing tumor' phenomenon (lympholysis).
Cytopathology is often negative due to sample degradation; MYD88 mutation analysis significantly increases sensitivity.
In OAL, if you see a 'Salmon Patch', biopsying the conjunctiva is often more diagnostic and less invasive than orbital imaging.
Rituximab is increasingly used as an alternative to radiation for OAL to avoid ocular surface toxicity.
Landmark Study: IELSG (International Extranodal Lymphoma Study Group) guidelines suggest intensive systemic therapy for combined ocular-CNS disease.
